doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

chapter: Meeting Joe and life with the Basie band
title: Hardships and loyalty of the Basie band; Joe waving it off
summary: Thirteen one-nighters were hard but the band loved to play, with Basie conducting by a nod; Joe still gets up at night to see the band off.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Do you find that that idea of big bands traveling like they did is kind of a lost thing now? There’s still a few around but, in fact we saw the Basie band about a month ago, but was it a hard life at that point? Because I always wanted to do that. And I always had maybe not a clear picture of what it was really like. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

I would think it was hard in the sense that, you know, 13 one-nighters in a row in different towns is pretty tough. So from the point of view of sleeping and eating it was hard. But I think that’s what they liked to do because they all loved to play. There was a tremendous spirit of loyalty among the Basie band. And it sort of shows in the way Basie conducts, you know. I mean he only had to point a finger or nod or something and that was his conducting. There was no waving his arms in front of the band. There was a great cohesion in the band. And I think they loved it. I think they enjoyed it. They were just a wonderful group of people.
There’s still that cohesion in the alumni I think.
I really think so. I don’t want to put words in your mouth, but you once told me about after Joe had left the band that he would get up in the middle of the night and go down and see it off.

Oh, yes, absolutely, absolutely. He used to, if the band was leaving at one in the morning to go to drive to Boston or to drive to Philadelphia or somewhere, he would get up and go down to the hotel and just wave them good-bye. You know you never leave the Basie band, to this day if they are within earshot, we’re there. You never leave the Basie band. They came back all the time. Joe does quite a lot of concerts with them still, which is fun.
